summary: To say how well, how fast, how early an action is done, Chinese puts the comment after the verb: Verb + 得 + (很) adjective. The idea that makes it click: 得 must touch the verb. An object, 了 or 不 can never sit between them, so the object is moved out of the way and 不 goes after 得. The same 得 after an adjective adds 'extremely': 热得很, 累得要命.

subs.label: Verb + 得 + 很 + adjective
subs.focus: No object. Learner must put 得 (not 的, 地, 了 or nothing) between verb and comment and keep it directly on the verb, also in past-time sentences. Classic mistakes: 他跑很快, 他很快跑, 他昨天来了得很晚. Keep a degree word (很, 非常, 真, 不太) before the adjective.

subs.label: Object present: repeat the verb
subs.focus: Sentence has an object or a verb-object word (游泳, 睡觉, 唱歌, 跳舞, 做饭, 开车). Learner must repeat the verb before 得: 说中文说得很好, 游泳游得很快. Classic mistake: 得 after the object (他说中文得很好, 他游泳得很快). Tile the two verbs separately, or blank the second verb.

subs.label: Object present: move it before the verb
subs.focus: Learner must put the object before the verb: 他中文说得很好, 这个菜你做得很好吃. Classic mistakes: 他说得很好中文, 他说得中文很好. Order items need alts: 他中文说得很好, 中文他说得很好 and 他说中文说得很好 are all correct, so cut tiles to limit what can be built.

subs.label: 不 goes after 得
subs.focus: The learner must put the negative on the comment: 说得不好, 睡得不太好. Classic mistakes: 不 before the verb (他不说得好), and 没 for past time (我昨天没睡得好). Include 不太 and 不怎么; never use 没太 after 得 as a wrong option. Do not use sentences where a negated verb plus a different structure would also be natural.

subs.label: Asking: 得怎么样, 得好不好, 得…吗
subs.focus: The learner must build the question on the part after 得: 考得怎么样, 说得好不好, 睡得好吗. Classic mistakes: A-not-A on the verb (他说不说得好), 吗 added to a 怎么样 or A-not-A question, and 很 kept inside A-not-A (说得很好不好). Also drill short answers: 说得很好 / 说得不太好.

subs.label: Adjective + 得 + 很 / 不得了 / 要命
subs.focus: Intensifier after an adjective or feeling verb: 热得很, 高兴得不得了, 累得要命. Learner must keep 得, add no 很 in front, and know 极了 and 死了 take no 得. Classic mistakes: 很热得很, 累要命 (好得极了 is heard: not judge-wrong). Use 要命 only for unpleasant things; never test 要命 against 不得了.

subs.label: 得 after the verb or 地 before it
subs.focus: Verb + 得 + adjective versus adjective + 地 + Verb; blank position must decide. Classic mistakes: 地 or 的 after the verb (他跑地很快, 他说的很好) and 地 for a judgment of skill, result or timing (他很好地说中文; 很早地来了 is only stiff, not wrong). Never use tiles where both a 地 and a 得 sentence are natural.

subs.label: 很 + adjective or Verb + 得 + adjective
subs.focus: Does the adjective describe the person or thing (他很高, 他的中文很好) or how an action goes (他跑得很快, 他中文说得很好)? Classic mistakes: English-style 他很好说中文, 她很漂亮写字, or dropping the verb (他中文得很好). Do not mark topic-comment 他跑步很快 as wrong: it is acceptable.

rules.rule: To comment on how an action is done, say the verb, then 得, then a degree word and the adjective. The comment comes after the verb, never before it.
rules.pattern: Subject + Verb + 得 + 很 / 非常 / 真 / 太 + Adjective

examples.py: tā pǎo de hěn kuài
tā chàng de fēi cháng hǎo
nǐ lái de tài zǎo le

rules.note: 很 here is usually just a filler, not a strong 'very'. A bare adjective (他跑得快) is possible but sounds like a comparison or an answer to a question, and out of context it can also be read as 'he is able to run fast', so use a degree word in plain statements.

rules.rule: 得 sticks to the verb. Do not put 了 between them, even when the action is in the past or already finished; a time word is enough.
rules.pattern: Subject + time + Verb + 得 + 很 + Adjective

examples.py: wǒ zuó tiān shuì de hěn wǎn
examples.en: I went to sleep very late yesterday.

examples.py: tā jīn tiān qǐ de hěn zǎo
wǒ men zuó tiān wán de hěn gāo xìng
examples.en: We had a great time yesterday.

rules.note: The 了 in 太…了 (来得太早了) belongs to 太 and sits at the end of the sentence; that one is fine.

rules.rule: If the verb has an object, 得 cannot follow the object. Say verb + object first, then say the verb again and add 得. Verb-object words such as 游泳, 睡觉, 唱歌, 跳舞, 做饭 and 开车 work the same way: repeat only the first character.
rules.pattern: Subject + Verb + Object + Verb + 得 + 很 + Adjective

examples.py: tā shuō zhōng wén shuō de hěn hǎo
tā xiě hàn zì xiě de hěn piào liang
wǒ dì di yóu yǒng yóu de hěn kuài
wǒ zuó tiān shuì jiào shuì de hěn wǎn
examples.en: I went to bed very late yesterday.

rules.note: You can also just drop the object part of a verb-object word when it adds nothing: 他游得很快, 我睡得很晚.

rules.rule: Instead of repeating the verb, you can put the object before the verb, right after the subject or at the very start of the sentence. Nothing follows the adjective.
rules.pattern: Subject + Object + Verb + 得 + 很 + Adjective

examples.py: tā zhōng wén shuō de hěn hǎo
zhè ge cài nǐ zuò de hěn hǎo chī
examples.en: You cooked this dish really well.

examples.py: zuò yè tā xiě de hěn rèn zhēn

rules.note: A third common version uses 的: 他的中文说得很好, 她的字写得很漂亮. All of these mean the same as the verb-copy sentence.

rules.rule: To say something is not done well, negate the adjective after 得 with 不. Standard usage does not put 不 or 没 in front of the verb, whatever the time.
rules.pattern: Subject + Verb + 得 + 不 / 不太 + Adjective

examples.py: tā shuō de bù hǎo
wǒ zuó tiān shuì de bù hǎo
examples.en: I didn't sleep well last night.

examples.py: tā kāi chē kāi de bù tài kuài

rules.note: Do not confuse this with the result complement, where 没 does go before the verb and there is no 得: 我昨天没睡好. After 得 the standard negator is 不 (不太, 不怎么); colloquial 没太 / 没怎么 + adjective is also heard there.

rules.rule: Ask about the part after 得: use 怎么样 for an open question, adjective + 不 + adjective or 吗 for yes or no. 怎么样 and A-not-A questions take no 吗, and A-not-A takes no 很.
rules.pattern: Subject + Verb + 得 + 怎么样 / Adjective + 不 + Adjective

examples.py: nǐ kǎo de zěn me yàng
tā zhōng wén shuō de hǎo bù hǎo
nǐ zuó tiān wǎn shang shuì de hǎo ma
examples.en: Did you sleep well last night?

rules.rule: Adjective + 得很 means 'really, very'. It is stronger than 很 + adjective, and you cannot use both at once.

examples.py: jīn tiān rè de hěn
nà r de dōng xi guì de hěn
tā zuì jìn máng de hěn
examples.en: He has been really busy lately.

rules.rule: For 'extremely', add 得不得了 or 得要命 after an adjective or a feeling verb. 得 is required and there is no 很 in front.
rules.pattern: Subject + Adjective + 得 + 不得了 / 要命

examples.py: tā gāo xìng de bù dé liǎo
wǒ jīn tiān lèi de yào mìng
wài miàn lěng de yào mìng

rules.note: 要命 is mostly used for unpleasant things (累, 冷, 疼, 忙), though people do say 喜欢得要命; 不得了 fits good and bad alike. 极了 and 死了 attach directly, with no 得: 好极了, 累死了 (好得极了 is heard in speech but is not standard).

rules.rule: Position decides the particle. A describing word before the verb is linked with 地 and tells the manner in which someone does something; a comment after the verb is linked with 得.
rules.pattern: Adjective + 地 + Verb / Verb + 得 + 很 + Adjective

examples.py: tā gāo xìng de xiào le
tā xiào de hěn gāo xìng
tā rèn zhēn de tīng lǎo shī shuō huà
examples.en: She listens carefully to the teacher.

rules.note: Both are pronounced de, so this is a writing choice. In casual writing native speakers often type 的 for either one; in this app only 得 after the verb and 地 before it are accepted.

rules.rule: When you are judging skill, result, speed or timing (well, badly, fast, early, late, clearly), use Verb + 得. These adjectives do not go before the verb with 地.
rules.pattern: Subject + Verb + 得 + 很 + 好 / 快 / 早 / 晚 / 清楚

examples.py: tā jīn tiān lái de hěn zǎo
lǎo shī shuō de hěn qīng chu
tā tiào wǔ tiào de hěn hǎo

rules.note: 很快 before a verb does exist, but it means 'soon, before long' (他很快就回来了), not 'at high speed'.

rules.rule: 很 + adjective alone describes what a person or thing is like. When the English says someone does something well, fast or badly, the verb must be there and the adjective goes after 得.
rules.pattern: Subject + 很 + Adjective / Subject + Verb + 得 + 很 + Adjective

examples.py: tā hěn gāo pǎo de yě hěn kuài
examples.en: He is tall and he also runs fast.

examples.py: tā de zhōng wén hěn hǎo
tā zhōng wén shuō de hěn hǎo

examples.zh: 我妈妈做饭做得很好吃。
examples.py: wǒ mā ma zuò fàn zuò de hěn hǎo chī
examples.en: My mum is a very good cook.

rules.note: Chinese also allows an activity as the topic followed by 很 + adjective: 他跑步很快, 她做饭很好吃. That is correct too. What is never possible is adjective first and verb after it, as in English 'good at speaking': 他很好说中文.

right.py: tā shuō zhōng wén shuō de hěn hǎo

contrasts.why: 得 must follow a verb, not an object. Repeat 说 after 中文, or move 中文 in front: 他中文说得很好.

right.py: wǒ dì di yóu yǒng yóu de hěn kuài

contrasts.why: 游泳 is verb 游 plus object 泳, so 得 after it is 得 after an object. Repeat 游, or just say 游得很快.
He does speak; what is negated is 'well'. 不 goes after 得, on the adjective.

right.py: wǒ zuó tiān shuì de bù hǎo
right.en: I didn't sleep well last night.

contrasts.why: Past time does not change the rule: still 不 after 得 (a few speakers say 没睡得好, but it is not standard). 没 before the verb works without 得, as a result complement: 没睡好.

right.py: tā zuó tiān lái de hěn wǎn

contrasts.why: Nothing can stand between the verb and 得, not even 了. 昨天 already shows it is past.
A verb cannot be followed directly by 很 + adjective. The link 得 is required.

right.py: tā chàng gē chàng de hěn hǎo

contrasts.why: 'Well' is a judgment of how the singing turns out, so it goes after the verb with 得. 很好地 + verb is written style for 'successfully' (很好地完成了任务), not for 'does something well'.

right.py: nǐ kǎo de zěn me yàng

contrasts.why: 怎么样 already makes it a question. 吗 is only for yes or no questions such as 你考得好吗？
得很 already gives the degree, so the adjective takes no 很 in front. Choose 很热 or 热得很.

right.py: wǒ jīn tiān lèi de yào mìng

contrasts.why: 要命 and 不得了 need 得 to attach to the adjective. Only 极了 and 死了 attach directly: 累死了.

cheat: How well, how fast, how early? Verb + 得 + 很 + adjective, comment after the verb.
得 touches the verb: no object, no 了, no 不 in between.
Got an object, or a word like 游泳, 睡觉, 唱歌? Repeat the verb (说中文说得) or move the object forward (中文说得).
Negative: 不 after 得 (说得不好), also for the past. Never 不说得 or 没说得.
Question: 得怎么样？ 得好不好？ 得好吗？ No 吗 with the first two.
After the verb write 得; before the verb write 地. 'Well, fast, early, late' go after the verb.
热得很, 累得要命, 高兴得不得了: keep 得, drop the 很 in front. 极了 and 死了 take no 得.
